key_equations_and_data: §4.1 Kirchhoff, opaque surface in LTE: eps(lambda,theta,phi) = alpha = 1 - rho(lambda,theta,phi), rho = directional-hemispherical reflectance (DHR = hemispherical integral of the BRDF at the view geometry; DHE = 1 - DHR per DIRSIG [R3]). Rule: author ONE spectral property per band, derive the other; never author two.

§4.4 general closure triple, per band: eps + rho + tau = 1. Tolerance 1e-6 absolute (§15 Tier-1 table line 1182; ir-sim-testing skill 'Kirchhoff closure 1e-6 absolute — data quality, not arithmetic'; thermal-materials skill Rule 1: fix the data, never loosen the tolerance).

§4.2 Level A Fresnel from complex index n~(lambda) = n + i k: Z = n~^2 - sin^2(theta_i); A = sqrt((|Z| + Re Z)/2); B = sgn(Im Z) * sqrt((|Z| - Re Z)/2); sqrt(Z) := A + jB (branch-safe: selects Im(k_z) > 0, passivity). r_perp = (cos theta - (A+jB)) / (cos theta + (A+jB)); r_par = ((A+jB) - n~^2 cos theta) / ((A+jB) + n~^2 cos theta); R_perp = |r_perp|^2, R_par = |r_par|^2; R = (R_perp + R_par)/2; eps(lambda,theta) = 1 - R(lambda,theta). Implementation must assert 0 <= R <= 1 (skill). Closed-form check independent of the A/B machinery: R(0) = ((n-1)^2 + k^2)/((n+1)^2 + k^2).

§4.2 Level A known answers: water at 10 um, n = 1.218, k = 0.0508 [R1]. Verified in this session with the spec's equations: R(0 deg) = 0.010180 (eps 0.9898); eps(60 deg) = 0.9612; eps(80 deg) = 0.6972; eps(89.9 deg) = 0.0122; hemispherical eps_h = 2*int eps(theta) cos sin dtheta = 0.9511. Bismuth is the second reference in [R1] (values not given in spec). Lossless n=1.5 Brewster null: R_par(atan 1.5) = 0 to ~1e-32. n=1,k=0: R = 0 at all angles. Strongly absorbing media show NO sharp TIR knee: R < 1 at every angle (§4.2 line 238).

§4.2 Level B empirical angular falloff: eps(theta) = eps0 * [1 - a * (1 - cos theta)^p], a ~ 0.15-0.35, p ~ 4-6 for painted metals and plastics; a -> 0 for rough dielectrics (asphalt, vegetation, fabric). Fit (a, p) once per material class against Level A and bake. Skill acceptance: max |eps_B - eps_A| < 0.02 over 0-70 deg. NOTE §13.5 kernel (line 1066) hard-codes p = 4 and carries only float2 (eps0, a) per material.
§4.2 Level C constant eps: permitted only for rough, high-emissivity surfaces (eps > 0.93) within +/-50 deg of normal. Vehicle bodies, glass, water are explicitly excluded.

§4.3 per-band roughness: IR lobe narrower/stronger than visible; optically smooth when sigma_rms << lambda/8. `roughness_per_band` must decrease with wavelength for smooth-class materials (example {nir 0.35, swir 0.30, mwir 0.18, lwir 0.12}); never reuse visible-band roughness. Numerical meaning of 'roughness' (GGX alpha vs RMS height in um) is NOT defined by the spec.

§4.4 semi-transparent materials: per-band triple (eps, rho, tau) with eps+rho+tau = 1; tau > 0 handled as a second ray in the SWIR/NIR path. Glass: eps_LWIR ~ 0.85-0.92 (opaque), transparent in SWIR/NIR. Skill test: glass returns tau > 0.5 in SWIR and tau ~ 0 in LWIR. Reference composition for the second ray (materials-owned, engine-free): L_out = eps*Lb(T_surf) + rho*L_env + tau*L_behind per band; identity: T_surf = T_env = T_behind = T  =>  L_out = Lb(T) for any closed triple.

§12.3 material schema (per-band SPECTRAL, not per-band scalar): materials.<name>.thermal{density_kg_m3, specific_heat_j_kgk, conductivity_w_mk, thickness_m, solar_absorptivity} ; optical{spectral_emissivity: 'spectra/<name>.csv' (lambda um, eps(lambda), 0.3-15 um), roughness_per_band{nir,swir,mwir,lwir}, angular_model{type: fresnel, n_k_file: 'nk/<name>.csv'}, transmittance_per_band{nir,swir,mwir,lwir}}. thermal-materials skill adds top-level `source: measured|literature|estimated` (mandatory in practice) and drops the `materials:` wrapper. Schema must also express angular_model variants {type: empirical, a, p} and {type: constant} — not shown in spec but required by §4.2 Levels B/C and the §13.5 kernel.

Band-effective (grey-within-band) emissivity — NOT written in the spec but required to reconcile §12.3 (spectral) with Appendix A item 3 (line 1388, 'emissivity is grey within a band') and the §13.5 kernel's scalar eps0: eps_B(T) = int R(lambda) eps(lambda) B(lambda,T) dlambda / int R(lambda) B(lambda,T) dlambda for energy detectors (bolometer, §3.1 energy form), and with B_q(lambda,T) (photon form, §3.1) for photon detectors (MWIR/SWIR/NIR). Same for tau_B and rho_B. Reference quadrature: Simpson on a 0.01 um grid (§3.2 b). The T at which to evaluate (300 K reference vs. tabulated eps_B(T)) is a decision (see ADRs).

Hemispherical emissivity for the thermal solver (§6.1 emitted term eps*sigma*T^4 and absorbed eps*Q_LW; §6.2 says eps is 'spectral; drives both heat balance and radiance'): eps_hemi(lambda) = 2 * int_0^{pi/2} eps(lambda,theta) cos theta sin theta dtheta; total eps_tot(T) = int eps_hemi(lambda) B(lambda,T) dlambda / (sigma T^4 / pi). For constant eps this is the identity; for Fresnel water at 10 um it is 0.951 vs 0.990 at normal incidence (computed this session).

§16.2 starting values (literature, NOT measurements; mark `source: literature`), columns eps_LWIR, eps_MWIR, alpha_sol, rho kg/m3, c_p J/kgK, k W/mK: asphalt dry 0.94/0.92/0.90/2200/920/0.75; concrete 0.92/0.90/0.65/2300/880/1.4; car paint black 0.90/0.88/0.94/7800/470/45; car paint white 0.90/0.88/0.28/7800/470/45; bare aluminium 0.09/0.06/0.15/2700/900/205; rusted steel 0.85/0.82/0.80/7800/470/45; glass windshield 0.88/0.85/0.10/2500/840/1.0; rubber tyre 0.95/0.94/0.94/1100/2000/0.16; human skin 0.98/0.97/0.65/1050/3500/0.37; cotton clothing 0.95/0.93/0.70/300/1300/0.06; vegetation leaf 0.97/0.96/0.50/700/3000/0.30; soil dry 0.92/0.90/0.75/1500/800/0.30; soil wet 0.96/0.95/0.85/2000/1500/1.5; water 0.96/0.98/0.93/1000/4180/0.60; snow 0.99/0.98/0.15/300/2100/0.20. No thickness_m, no NIR/SWIR eps, no roughness, no tau, no angular parameters are given. Paint example thickness_m = 0.0012 (§12.3).

Thermal derived quantities the material must supply to the thermal area (§6.1, §6.3, §6.4): C = rho * c_p * delta (J m^-2 K^-1); thermal inertia P = sqrt(k rho c_p); R_12 = delta_1/(2k) + delta_2/(2k); alpha_sol used as ABSORPTIVITY (absorbed = alpha_sol * Q_sol, §6.1 line 363) — the field is not albedo.

Skill Rule 2 finish taxonomy (thermal-materials lines 38-43): painted eps_LWIR 0.88-0.93 (colour changes solar_absorptivity, not eps); bare/polished metal 0.05-0.15 (a mirror); oxidised 0.75-0.90; coated exhaust/heat shield 0.20-0.85 (measure). Library is organised by surface finish, with alloy as a second-order substrate correction.

Data files: data/nk/<material>.csv (lambda um, n, k; source refractiveindex.info, source URL recorded in the material YAML and file header) [§4.2, skill line 96]; data/spectra/<material>.csv (lambda um, eps(lambda), 0.3-15 um) [§12.3]. Both must be monotonic in lambda, in micrometres, and cover every configured band (7.5-13.5 for the Boson config).

Kernel-facing packed table (§13.3 'DiffuseAlbedo or material-ID' AOV, uint8/float; §13.5 `const float2* matEps` = (eps0, a); §14 Unreal 'material parameter collection / texture atlas'): per material index -> per band {eps0, a, p, rho_B, tau_B, roughness} plus thermal {rho, c_p, k, thickness, alpha_sol}, all float32 (non-negotiable #2), with a reserved 'unmapped' sentinel index rendered magenta (skill 'USD import problem'). conftest.py fixes the pixel-side key as int32 `material_id`.

USD mapping layer resolution order (skill lines 117-122): (1) explicit `thermal:material` USD attribute override; (2) semantic class (car_body, road, pedestrian) from the semantics schema; (3) material-name pattern (*paint*, *glass*, *chrome*, *rubber*); (4) loud default + recorded miss. Deliverables: scripts/audit_materials.py (per-prim misses grouped/counted, coverage %, CI threshold) and a magenta debug AOV for unmapped surfaces.

work_items.title: Material schema (pydantic) + YAML loader with author-one-derive-the-rest closure
work_items.description: Create `irsim/config/materials.py` (schema) and `irsim/materials/library.py` (loader). Schema: `source` (measured|literature|estimated, required), `thermal{density_kg_m3, specific_heat_j_kgk, conductivity_w_mk, thickness_m, solar_absorptivity}`, `optical{spectral_emissivity | spectral_reflectance (exactly one), roughness_per_band, angular_model (discriminated union: fresnel{n_k_file} | empirical{a,p} | constant), transmittance_per_band}`. Band keys are free strings validated later against the sensor configs (bands are data, not code). Loader resolves file paths relative to `data/`, derives rho_B = 1 - eps_B - tau_B per band, and refuses any input where eps_B + tau_B > 1. Provides `MaterialThermal` (the one object the thermal area consumes) and `MaterialOptical`. Accept both the §12.3 `materials:` wrapper and the skill's bare-key form, or pick one in the ADR. Docstrings cite §4.1/§4.4/§12.3.

work_items.title: Level B empirical angular model and per-class (a, p) fitter against Level A

work_items.description: Create `irsim/materials/angular.py`: `emissivity_empirical(eps0, a, p, cos_theta)` = eps0 * (1 - a * (1 - cos)^p), and `fit_empirical(eps_A(theta), theta_grid, p_choices=(4,5,6))` returning (eps0, a, p, max_residual) by least squares over 0-70 deg with bounds a in [0, 0.5]. work_items.description: Create `irsim/materials/table.py`: `MaterialTable.from_library(library, bands)` producing contiguous float32 arrays indexed by a stable integer id: per band `eps0[m, b]`, `a[m, b]`, `p[m, b]`, `rho[m, b]`, `tau[m, b]`, `roughness[m, b]`, plus thermal columns; index 0 reserved for UNMAPPED (flagged, rendered magenta downstream). Serialise to `data/lut/<library_hash>_materials.npz` with a JSON sidecar (config hash, band list, index->name). This is what the Warp/SPG kernels upload via `cuda.static`.
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: test_closure_survives_float32_packing: for every (m, b), |eps0 + rho + tau - 1| < 1e-6 after packing to float32 (float32 epsilon ~6e-8 keeps this comfortably inside tolerance; a float16 pack would fail at ~1e-3).
test_all_arrays_float32_or_int32: dtype assertions on every array (non-negotiable #2).
test_round_trip_by_name: table[index_of('car_paint_black')].eps0['lwir'] equals the library's eps_B to 1e-6; index_of on an unknown name raises.

test_sentinel_index_zero_is_unmapped: row 0 has eps = NaN-free sentinel values and `is_unmapped[0]` is True; conftest `material_id` zeros therefore point at UNMAPPED unless the fixture is updated — the test asserts the fixture is updated to a real material.
test_stale_table_detected: changing one YAML value changes the sidecar hash so a stale npz is rejected on load.

work_items.title: Engine-free reference for the (eps, rho, tau) surface composition including the second ray
spec_refs: §12.2 line 900 'enable glass transmission in the material resolver'
work_items.description: Create `irsim/materials/surface.py`: `surface_radiance(eps, rho, tau, Lb_surface, L_env, L_behind)` = eps*Lb_surface + rho*L_env + tau*L_behind, vectorised, float32-preserving; L_behind defaults to L_env when tau == 0 so LWIR-only callers need no second ray. This is the materials-owned oracle the scene-radiance kernel (isaac area) reproduces; it uses `band_radiance_tophat` for tests and takes band radiances as inputs so it does not depend on the LUT.
depends_on: radiometry: existing `band_radiance_tophat` (present); later the band LUT for speed
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: test_isothermal_enclosure_identity: for ANY closed triple, with Lb_surface = L_env = L_behind = Lb(T), output == Lb(T) to 1e-12 relative (a surface in an isothermal cavity is indistinguishable from a blackbody — fails if closure or a coefficient is wrong).
test_tau_zero_reduces_to_opaque: equals eps*Lb + (1-eps)*L_env to 1e-12 (the §13.5 kernel form).
test_glass_shows_driver_in_swir_and_itself_in_lwir: with the v0 glass material, dL_out/dL_behind == tau_swir (> 0.5) and == tau_lwir (< 0.01); dL_out/dLb_surface == eps_lwir (~0.88).

test_cold_sky_reflection_sign: for aluminium (eps 0.09) with L_env = Lb(233 K) and T_surf = 300 K, apparent radiance < Lb(250 K) (the 'roofs read cold' phenomenon, §4.3); a model that ignores rho fails.

work_items.title: Engine-free USD material-mapping resolver (override -> semantic -> name pattern -> loud default)

work_items.description: Create `irsim/materials/mapping.py`: input is a plain list of `PrimRecord(path, material_name, semantic_class, override)` (no USD types), output `MappingResult(assignments: dict[path, material_id], misses: list[PrimRecord], coverage: float)`. tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: test_precedence_override_beats_semantic_beats_pattern: a prim with all three set resolves to the override; with two, to the semantic; with one, to the pattern.

test_known_names_resolve: 'Car_Paint_Metallic_Red' -> car_paint_*, 'Windshield_Glass' -> glass_windshield, 'Chrome_Trim' -> bare_aluminium (finish taxonomy, skill Rule 2), 'Tire_Rubber' -> rubber_tyre.
test_unknown_is_reported_not_defaulted: 'Mystery_Mat_07' appears in misses with sentinel id 0, and coverage drops accordingly; a resolver that returns a real material here fails.

work_items.title: scripts/audit_materials.py + Isaac USD stage walker feeding the resolver
work_items.description: `scripts/audit_materials.py` accepts either a USD stage path (requires Isaac/pxr, imports only inside `irsim_isaac.materials_usd`) or a JSON prim dump (engine-free path), runs MAT-10, prints misses grouped and counted with coverage %, exits non-zero below the threshold. `irsim_isaac/materials_usd.py` walks the stage, reads bound material names, `semantic:Semantics` params, and the `thermal:material` custom attribute (name to be fixed by ADR) into `PrimRecord`s, and writes the resolved index back as a per-prim primvar for the material-ID AOV.

tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: unit: test_audit_from_json_dump: a fixture dump with 3 known and 2 unknown names yields coverage 0.6, lists both unknowns, exit code 1 at threshold 0.9.
integration (@isaac): test_audit_sample_stage: a checked-in 4-prim USDA test stage with known bindings resolves all four; adding a fifth unbound prim is reported as a miss.
integration (@isaac): test_override_attribute_wins: a prim whose visible material says *glass* but carries `thermal:material = car_paint_black` resolves to paint.

work_items.title: Material-ID AOV binding and magenta unmapped debug AOV in Isaac Sim 6.0
work_items.description: In `irsim_isaac/pipeline/material_id.py`: emit a per-pixel integer material index from the per-prim primvar written by MAT-11 through whichever AOV the experiment in the ambiguities list shows is exact (custom primvar AOV, semantic-segmentation remap, or DiffuseAlbedo encoding), nearest-sampled (no AA blending of IDs), and bind the MAT-08 table on the GPU once via `cuda.static` / a warp array. Add the magenta debug output for sentinel 0.
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: integration (@isaac): test_material_id_is_integer_exact: a 3-material test scene rendered at 4x supersampling; every pixel's decoded id is in {ids of the three prims, 0}; zero pixels carry a non-integer or blended value (an AA-interpolated id at an edge is a wrong material, not a small error).

work_items.title: Hemispherical (band and total) emissivity from the directional model, for the thermal solver
spec_refs: §6.2 'spectral; drives both heat balance and radiance'
§16.2 (table values fall between normal and hemispherical)
work_items.description: Create `irsim/materials/hemispherical.py`: `hemispherical_emissivity(material, lambda_or_band)` = 2 * int_0^{pi/2} eps(theta) cos theta sin theta dtheta via Gauss-Legendre in cos theta; `total_hemispherical_emissivity(material, T)` integrates over lambda with B(lambda,T)/(sigma T^4/pi) weighting. Exposed on `MaterialThermal` so the thermal area never reuses the band directional eps by accident. Records in the ADR which quantity the §16.2 scalars are taken to be.
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: test_constant_eps_identity: Level C material gives eps_hemi == eps to 1e-12 and eps_tot(T) == eps to 1e-12 for any T.
test_water_10um_hemispherical_known_answer: Fresnel water gives eps_hemi = 0.951 +/- 0.002 (independent midpoint quadrature, N = 20000, computed this session) and eps_hemi < eps(0) = 0.990.
test_metal_hemispherical_exceeds_normal: aluminium (25.3, 89.8): eps_hemi (0.015) > eps(0) (0.012) — sign of the difference flips for metals; a model that assumes monotone falloff fails.
test_quadrature_convergence: Gauss-Legendre 16-point vs 64-point agree to 1e-6 for every library material.

test_thermal_sensitivity_bound: for water, an equilibrium-temperature solve with eps = 0.990 vs 0.951 differs by > 0.3 K under a cold clear sky (justifies why the solver must not use the normal-incidence value).

decisions_needing_adr.title: Band-effective emissivity convention (how spectral eps(lambda) becomes the scalar the kernel uses)
decisions_needing_adr.why: §12.3 mandates spectral authoring, Appendix A item 3 declares eps grey within a band, and the §13.5 kernel consumes one eps0 per material; the reduction that connects them is not written anywhere. The choice fixes a permanent error: Planck weighting at a fixed T_ref makes hot objects (exhaust at 500 K) use a slightly wrong eps; ignoring the photon/energy distinction biases MWIR/SWIR by a band-dependent amount.
options: Weight by B(lambda, 300 K) (energy) for bolometer bands and B_q(lambda, 300 K) for photon bands; single scalar per material per band; error bounded by a test that reports max |eps_B(200 K) - eps_B(1000 K)| across the library
Tabulate eps_B(T) alongside the Planck LUT (adds a second LUT per material per band; exact for non-grey spectra; raises kernel table size)
Unweighted mean of eps(lambda) across the band (simplest; wrong by up to a few percent for sloped spectra)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Angular-model level per material class and the baked (a, p) values
decisions_needing_adr.why: §4.2 says pick per class, not globally, and the §13.5 kernel hard-codes Level B with p = 4. Level B cannot represent metals (eps rises with angle) or low-n materials, so which materials get Level A in the kernel, and whether p is per-material or fixed, changes the kernel argument layout (float2 vs float3/float4 per material) — a decision that outlives every commit touching the kernel.
options: Level A only for water/glass/bare metal (n/k tables, evaluated per pixel or via a small angular LUT); Level B with per-material p for painted/plastic; Level C for rough dielectrics
Level B everywhere with p fixed at 4 as in §13.5 (two shader instructions; accept > 0.02 error on metals and document it)
Precompute a per-material eps(cos theta) 1-D LUT (e.g. 64 entries float32) so the kernel is level-agnostic and the CPU chooses the level

decisions_needing_adr.title: What the §16.2 scalar emissivities mean, and which source wins when n/k Fresnel disagrees with the table
decisions_needing_adr.why: Verified numerically: Fresnel from bulk n/k gives water eps(0) = 0.990 / eps_hemi = 0.951 against the table's 0.96, and aluminium 0.012-0.015 against 0.09. Real bare metal has an oxide layer and roughness the bulk n/k does not capture. The library must declare whether a scalar is normal-incidence, hemispherical, or an effective measured value, and whether Fresnel-derived eps is rescaled to match the table (an 'effective n/k' fit) or the table is discarded for Fresnel materials.
options: Table values are treated as effective near-normal band emissivity; for Level A materials, fit an effective k (or a thin-film/roughness factor) so eps(0) matches the table, keep the Fresnel angular shape
Trust n/k for Level A materials and mark the §16.2 row as superseded; accept eps_Al ~ 0.01 (a perfect mirror) until measured
Store both: `eps_normal` and `eps_hemispherical` explicitly per band, derived from the chosen model, with the thermal solver reading only the hemispherical one

decisions_needing_adr.title: Material file layout and data directory conventions
decisions_needing_adr.why: §12.3 shows a `materials:` wrapper (implying one library file); the skill shows bare top-level keys (implying one file per material); CLAUDE.md says the closure test 'walks the whole material library'. Also, §12.3 paths like `spectra/car_paint_black.csv` collide with the sensor config's `spectra/boson_vox.csv` in `data/spectra/`. Whatever is chosen becomes the on-disk contract for every asset anyone adds.
options: One YAML per material in configs/materials/, bare key, `source` required; emissivity spectra in data/spectra/materials/, detector responses in data/spectra/responses/ (sensor config already writes 'responses/boson_vox.csv' in §12.2 line 832 but 'spectra/boson_vox.csv' in the actual file — pick one)
Single configs/materials/library.yaml with the §12.3 wrapper
One YAML per material AND a generated index file with content hash, mirroring the LUT sidecar approach

decisions_needing_adr.title: Roughness semantics and its deferral at L2
decisions_needing_adr.why: §4.3/§12.3 require per-band roughness but never define the number (GGX alpha? RMS height in um with the lambda/8 rule? Beckmann sigma?), and the L2 sky-view-factor reflection (§5.3a, §13.5) never reads it. Authoring a number with undefined meaning now means re-authoring the whole library when option 2-4 of §13.7 lands.
options: Define roughness_per_band as a unitless microfacet alpha in [0,1] (GGX), document the lambda/8 derivation rule from an RMS height, leave it unconsumed at L2 and record that explicitly
Author RMS height sigma_h in um once (band-independent, physical) and derive per-band alpha via the sigma/lambda ratio in code — fewer numbers to author, one formula to validate
Defer the field entirely until §13.7 option 2+ exists (violates §4.4's 'schema must express it from day one' spirit for tau, but tau and roughness are separable)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Semi-transparent tau: scalar-per-band vs spectral, and where L_behind comes from
decisions_needing_adr.why: §12.3 makes tau per-band scalar while eps is spectral, so closure at spectral resolution is ill-defined; and the 'second ray' (§4.4) is an engine capability that LWIR-first work will not have. The choice determines whether MWIR glass (partially transmitting 3-4.5 um) is representable.
options: Spectral tau(lambda) file optional; scalar per band accepted and expanded to a flat spectrum; closure enforced on band-effective values only; L_behind = L_env until a second ray exists (documented approximation)
Spectral everything (eps and tau curves mandatory) with closure enforced per wavelength sample
Scalar per band only, no spectral tau ever (simplest, blocks spectral MWIR glass)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Mapping-layer default behaviour and CI coverage threshold
decisions_needing_adr.why: The skill demands a loud default and a CI-failing coverage threshold; the number chosen (e.g. 95%) and whether an unmapped prim renders as sentinel magenta radiance (poisoning downstream statistics) or is dropped from validation metrics affects every dataset generated.
options: Sentinel index 0 -> magenta in debug AOV and eps = 1, tau = 0 (blackbody) in the physics path so unmapped objects are at least energy-conserving; CI threshold 95%
Sentinel -> NaN radiance so any downstream metric fails loudly; CI threshold 100% on curated scenes
Fallback to a 'generic_painted' material with a logged warning (explicitly rejected by the skill; listed for completeness)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Provenance and licensing of checked-in n/k and emissivity data
decisions_needing_adr.why: refractiveindex.info aggregates datasets under varied licences; ECOSTRESS/ASTER spectral libraries have their own terms. Checked-in CSVs outlive commits and are redistributed with the repo.
options: Check in small CSV extracts with a `# source:` header citing the original paper (data are facts; cite the measurement), record licence per file
Download at `make data` time from a pinned URL with a hash, keep only the hash in git
Vendor only public-domain datasets (Hale & Querry water, Rakić aluminium) and mark everything else `estimated` with synthetic flat spectra

decisions_needing_adr.title: Fresnel specular R(theta) used as DHR for smooth materials (rough-surface DHR not modelled)
decisions_needing_adr.why: §4.1 defines rho as the hemispherically integrated BRDF but §4.2 uses the specular Fresnel reflectance directly as 1 - eps. That is exact only for optically smooth surfaces; for rough surfaces the DHR differs and eps(theta) is flatter. Choosing to ignore this is the L2 approximation and needs to be on record with the error it introduces (a few percent in eps for intermediate roughness).
options: Accept specular Fresnel as DHR for Level A materials (smooth by construction: water, glass, polished metal, gloss paint) and use Level B/C for anything rough; document the error band
Implement a microfacet DHR integral (GGX/Beckmann with the per-band roughness) as the Level A+ path — makes roughness consumed and closes the §4.1/§4.2 gap at the cost of a 2-D LUT per material

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The band-effective emissivity formula is absent from the spec (see ADR 1). Its magnitude matters: for a realistic sloped spectrum the difference between energy-weighted, photon-weighted and unweighted means can exceed the 0.02 Level-B budget.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Implement MAT-02 with all three reductions behind a flag; run the library and print max spread per material per band; if any exceeds 0.01, the ADR must pick the Planck-weighted form and the kernel must not take an unweighted mean.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: §13.5 hard-codes Level B with p = 4 and a float2 (eps0, a) per material; §4.2 says fit p in 4-6 per class; the skill's fit criterion is 0.02 over 0-70 deg. If p = 4 cannot meet 0.02 for glass or paint, the kernel signature must change (float3/float4) before any SPG or Warp code is written.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: MAT-05 fitter run over water, glass proxy, paint proxy with p locked at 4 versus free; report residuals. Decide the kernel layout from the numbers, not from the sketch.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: §16.2 scalar emissivities match neither normal-incidence nor hemispherical Fresnel from bulk n/k (water 0.96 vs 0.990/0.951; aluminium 0.09 vs 0.012/0.015). The table does not say what it tabulates.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Compute eps(0), eps_hemi, and eps(50 deg) for every Level-A material from its n/k table and diff against §16.2; write the ADR from the diff table. For aluminium, check whether a thin Al2O3 overlayer (n ~ 1.6, k ~ 0.1 at 10 um) or a roughness factor reproduces 0.09 before deciding to override.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: sgn(0) in the A/B branch rule is undefined for lossless media with Re(Z) < 0 (n < 1, beyond the critical angle). With sgn(0) = 0 the form gives sqrt(Z) = 0, which still yields R = 1 (correct TIR reflectance) but wrong phase; with sgn(0) = +1 it gives the textbook sqrt. Only matters for n < 1 materials (reststrahlen bands, some metals near plasma edges) and only if phase or polarisation is ever used.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Verified this session: n = 0.5, k = 0 at 60 deg gives R = 1.0 with sgn(0) = 0. Document the convention in MAT-03's docstring and add the n < 1 case to the bounded-sweep test.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The spec's r_par has the opposite overall sign to the usual textbook convention (r_par = (n~^2 cos - sqrt Z)/(n~^2 cos + sqrt Z)). Irrelevant for R = |r|^2; would matter for polarimetric work (Appendix A item 5 says out of scope).
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Brewster-null test in MAT-03 passes with either sign; note in the docstring which convention is implemented so a future polarisation extension does not inherit a silent sign.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Data directory collision: §12.3 puts material emissivity spectra at `spectra/<material>.csv`; the sensor config and ir-radiometry skill put detector response curves in `data/spectra/` too (and §12.2 line 832 says `responses/boson_vox.csv` while the actual file says `spectra/boson_vox.csv`). A loader that globs data/spectra will mix the two.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Decide the layout in the ADR (materials/ vs responses/ subdirectories), fix the sensor YAML path to match, and add a test that every spectral CSV declares its kind in a header.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Roughness is required by the schema but has no numerical definition and no consumer at L2 (sky-view-factor blend ignores it). Values authored now may be meaningless later.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Write the definition in the ADR before authoring MAT-07; add a schema test that roughness is in the declared range; grep the L2 kernel to confirm it is intentionally unread and say so in README limitations.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Closure is ill-defined at spectral resolution when eps is spectral and tau is per-band scalar (§12.3). The library-walk test must state on which quantities it asserts eps + rho + tau = 1.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: MAT-01/MAT-07: assert closure on band-effective values (after MAT-02 reduction) and, when a spectral tau file exists, additionally per wavelength sample; document both in the test docstring.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Glass in MWIR: §12.1 says 'opaque-ish', §4.4 gives only LWIR (opaque) and SWIR/NIR (transparent). Soda-lime glass transmits partially between 3 and ~4.5 um for windshield thickness, so tau_mwir is neither 0 nor 0.5 and depends on thickness.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Compute Beer-Lambert internal transmittance from the checked-in glass k(lambda) over 5 mm, band-average over 3-5 um with B(300 K) weighting, and set tau_mwir from that number; record it in the glass YAML with `source: literature` and the calculation.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Isaac Sim 6.0: it is not established which AOV can carry an exact integer material id. §13.3 hedges 'DiffuseAlbedo or material-ID, uint8/float'; SPG stdlib nodes do not support SINT/UINT textures; the §13.5 kernel reads the id via tex2D<float>; conftest uses int32. An anti-aliased or filtered id at object edges is a wrong material, not a small error.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Before MAT-12: render a 3-prim scene, enumerate annotators available on the render product (semantic segmentation, primvar-driven AOVs, DiffuseAlbedo), read back each candidate at 1x and 4x supersampling, histogram the values; accept only a channel whose histogram has exactly N+1 distinct values with no edge blending. Record the finding in the MAT-12 ADR.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The `thermal:material` USD override attribute name and the semantic-class source are unspecified. Isaac Replicator's semantics API and the `semantic:Semantics:params:*` attribute layout changed across 4.x/5.x, and 6.0 deprecates `isaacsim.sensors.camera` in favour of `isaacsim.sensors.experimental.rtx`.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: In a 6.0 session, author a prim with `customData`/attribute `thermal:material` and a Replicator semantic label, print the USD attributes via `prim.GetAttributes()`, and fix the names in the mapping ADR; write the MAT-11 integration test against those exact names.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Specular Fresnel R(theta) is used as the DHR (§4.1 vs §4.2). For rough materials this overstates the angular falloff; the spec routes those to Level C so the practical impact is confined to intermediate-roughness surfaces (matte paint, weathered plastics).
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: For a paint proxy, compare eps(theta) from specular Fresnel with a Beckmann/GGX DHR integral at alpha = 0.12 (the §12.3 LWIR value); if the difference exceeds 0.02 at 60 deg, the ADR must say so and Level B fits should target the DHR curve, not the specular one.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The thermal solver needs total hemispherical emissivity; the radiance path needs band directional emissivity. §6.2's single symbol eps invites using the LWIR band value in the energy balance.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: MAT-13's sensitivity test: solve equilibrium T for water with eps = 0.990 vs 0.951 under a clear-sky night forcing and show the difference (> 0.3 K expected); make `MaterialThermal` expose only the hemispherical quantity so the wrong one is not reachable from the thermal area.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Band names (nir/swir/mwir/lwir) appear as literal keys in §12.3; encoding them as an Enum in the schema would violate 'bands are data, not code' and block e.g. a second LWIR band with a different response.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Schema test: a material declaring an extra band key `lwir_wide` loads without code change; the library-walk test takes the band list from configs/sensors, not from a constant.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The existing unit suite could not be executed in this environment (no pytest/numpy in the default interpreter, no venv). The 'green' baseline is unverified here.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: `make install && make check` before the first materials commit; if radiometry tests fail, fix or report before building on them.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: float32 packing of the material table: closure at 1e-6 after float32 is comfortable (~1e-7 worst case) but a future fp16 table would fail silently at ~1e-3; the isaac side might be tempted to use fp16 textures for the material table.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: MAT-08 dtype test plus a deliberate negative test that packs to float16 and asserts the closure test fails, so the guard is known to be live.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Bismuth is named as the second [R1] validation material but no n/k values are quoted in the spec.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Pull n/k for Bi at 10 um from refractiveindex.info, add to data/nk with source, and add a second known-answer Fresnel test alongside water once the [R1] curve is available for comparison.

non_negotiables_touched: #1 Engine-free physics core: everything in MAT-01..MAT-10 and MAT-13 is pure Python + NumPy under src/irsim/materials and src/irsim/config; the USD stage walker (MAT-11) and the material-ID AOV binding (MAT-12) live in src/irsim_isaac. Enforced automatically by tests/unit/test_layering.py (rglob over src/irsim, forbids omni/pxr/isaacsim/warp/carb). The mapping resolver is deliberately designed on plain PrimRecord dataclasses so it is testable without pxr.

#2 float32 or better wherever temperature or radiance flows: the packed MaterialTable (MAT-08) stores every array as float32; `directional_emissivity` (MAT-06) and `surface_radiance` (MAT-09) preserve float32 inputs; spectra/LUT sidecars are written float32; the reference computations run in float64. Enforced by dtype assertions in tests/unit/test_material_table.py, test_directional_emissivity.py, and a negative float16 test that must fail closure.

#4 Kirchhoff closure eps + rho + tau = 1 to 1e-6 for every material in every band: the schema (MAT-01) makes it impossible to author both eps and rho; rho is derived; the library-walk test tests/unit/test_material_library_closure.py (MAT-07) iterates every YAML in configs/materials over the union of declared and sensor-configured bands; MAT-08 re-asserts closure after float32 packing; MAT-09's isothermal-enclosure identity fails if the composition breaks closure.

#3 (noise in radiance space), #5 (aperture factor) and #6 (single WeatherSeries) are not touched by this area: materials add no noise, define no aperture, and read no weather. The only contact with #6 is that `MaterialThermal` (MAT-01/MAT-13) is the single object the thermal solver consumes, which keeps thermal properties from being authored twice.
spec_internal_inconsistencies: §12.3 line 904 requires materials to be 'per-band spectral, not per-band scalar', but §16.2 lines 1262-1278 supplies only per-band scalars (LWIR and MWIR columns only; no NIR/SWIR), and Appendix A item 3 line 1388 states 'emissivity is grey within a band'. The spectral-to-band reduction that reconciles the three is not written anywhere in the spec.

§12.3 lines 906-920 wraps materials in a `materials:` key; thermal-materials skill lines 136-150 shows a bare top-level key and adds a mandatory `source:` field that §12.3 does not have. CLAUDE.md says 'one test walks the whole material library', which presumes a layout neither document fixes.
